instructions: Configuration validated. DNS, certificate files and external connectivity have not been tested; no running settings have changed.
Update Workbench in Apps first. Keep the existing /data volume, model mounts and container settings.
Point these names at your reverse proxy: eugene.example.org, workbench.example.org
Eugene's sign-in address is https://eugene.example.org/oidc. External sign-in uses it automatically unless you have explicitly saved another address.
Use https://eugene.example.org/inference/v1 as the model API base URL. It shares Eugene's proxy host and port, with its own network rules and API keys.
Create one proxy host per name, preserving Host. Forward them all to Eugene on HTTP port 8088. Require HTTPS for browser connections.

Only the proxy addresses entered here may connect. Use the proxy's address as Eugene sees it: on a shared Docker network, its address on that network, not its LAN address. The proxy must set X-Forwarded-Proto to https and add the visitor's address to X-Forwarded-For.

Put Eugene and your proxy on one Docker network and give the proxy a fixed address there, matching this setup. Eugene's other ports need not be published for the proxy. Use HTTPS transport across machines.
Enrolled machines keep reaching this one at its control port (8083 in the container), so keep that port published while other machines are enrolled.

Apply from this page: Eugene saves it and restarts. Then open https://eugene.example.org and sign in within 15 minutes, or Eugene goes back to how it was. Workbench's sign-in address follows by itself; its chats and sign-ins are kept.
